examples.en: Don't count on luck; prepare hard.

examples.ko: 시험에 붙은 건 요행이 아니라 노력 덕분이에요.
examples.en: Passing the exam wasn't a fluke; it was thanks to effort.
He avoided a major accident by sheer luck.

examples.ko: 요행만 믿고 일하면 오래 못 가요.
examples.en: If you work relying only on luck, you won't last long.

examples.ko: 복권 당첨 같은 요행은 자주 오지 않아요.
examples.en: A lucky break like winning the lottery doesn't come often.

examples.ko: 요행에 기대는 사람은 결국 후회하게 돼요.
examples.en: People who lean on luck end up regretting it.

explain: '행운'과 달리 노력 없이 얻은 운이라는 느낌이 있어서 '요행을 바라다'처럼 조금 부정적으로 자주 써요. '요행이 아니라 실력이에요'처럼 실력과 대비해서도 말해요.

phrases.example: 그는 요행으로 합격했다고 말하지만 사실 열심히 공부했어요.
phrases.en: He says he passed by luck, but he actually studied hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노력과 상관없이 운으로 이루었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something was achieved by luck, regardless of effort.

phrases.example: 이번에는 요행이 따라서 좋은 자리를 얻었어요.
phrases.en: Luck was on my side this time, and I got a good seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻하지 않게 운이 좋았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you were unexpectedly lucky.

phrases.example: 요행만 바라면 좋은 결과를 얻기 어려워요.
phrases.en: If you only hope for luck, it's hard to get good results.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노력하지 않고 운만 기대하는 태도를 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize relying on luck without making an effort.

explain_en: Unexpected luck without effort; often looked down on. Unlike '행운', it suggests luck gained without effort, so it often has a slightly negative tone, as in '요행을 바라다'. It is also used in contrast with skill, as in '요행이 아니라 실력이에요'.

t90.ax: Don't count on luck; prepare hard.

en: all or nothing; having nothing to lose

examples.en: It's all or nothing, so I'll see it through to the end.

examples.ko: 이제 와서 물러설 수 없으니 이판사판이에요.
examples.en: I can't back out now, so it's do or die.
He charged in with nothing to lose.

examples.ko: 회사가 망하기 직전이라 이판사판의 심정으로 신제품을 냈어요.
examples.en: The company was about to fail, so they released a new product in a do-or-die spirit.
I took the exam thinking it was all or nothing.
It's all or nothing anyway, so what is there to worry about?

explain: 막다른 곳에서 '될 대로 되라, 끝까지 해 보자'는 마음으로 나설 때 써요. 주로 '이판사판이다', '이판사판으로'처럼 쓰고, 조금 거친 입말 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: I made a desperate, all-in request directly to the boss.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잃을 것이 없다는 마음으로 행동에 나설 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when acting with a nothing-to-lose attitude.

phrases.en: I took the exam with a 'do or die' mindset.
phrases.nuance_ko: 각오를 말할 때 마음을 나타내는 말과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a word for mindset to express determination.

phrases.example: 어차피 안 되면 이판사판이에요, 한번 해 봐요.
phrases.en: If it doesn't work anyway, it's all or nothing, so let's give it a try.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 물러설 곳이 없다는 상황을 문장 끝에서 말할 때 써요. 입말이라 조금 거친 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used at the end of a sentence to say there is no way back. It is spoken language with a slightly rough feel.

explain_en: You use it when you are cornered and decide to go all in, with a 'come what may' attitude. It mostly appears as '이판사판이다' or '이판사판으로', and has a slightly rough, spoken feel.

en: to be content with what one has; to be self-sufficient

examples.en: It's a small house, but I live contentedly.
He is a person content with his present life.

examples.ko: 지금 성적에 자족하지 말고 계속 노력하세요.
examples.en: Don't settle for your current grades; keep trying.
His pay is small, but he is content, so he doesn't complain.
If you rest on a good result, you won't improve.
With a contented heart, you feel less anxious.

explain: 밖의 조건과 상관없이 지금 상태에 스스로 만족한다는 느낌이에요. 문맥에 따라 '자족하며 살다'처럼 좋은 뜻도 되고, '자족하면 발전이 없다'처럼 현재에 안주한다는 부정적인 뜻도 돼요.

phrases.en: I think a self-contented life is a happy one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가진 것에 만족하며 사는 모습을 좋은 뜻으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in a positive sense for living content with what one has.

phrases.en: If you are complacent with the present, it is hard to improve.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 상태에 머문다는 부정적인 느낌으로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can carry a negative sense of staying where one is.
phrases.en_equiv: to be complacent with the present

phrases.example: 그는 작은 성공에 자족하지 않고 계속 노력했어요.
phrases.en: He was not satisfied with a small success and kept working hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금에 만족하지 않고 더 나아가려는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone who keeps pushing further instead of settling.

explain_en: About contentment with your situation, an inner attitude, not about supplies. It suggests being satisfied with your current state regardless of outside conditions. Depending on context it can be positive ('자족하며 살다') or negative, meaning complacent ('자족하면 발전이 없다').

examples.en: On weekends I rest well at home and recharge.
During my vacation I recharged my body and mind.
Walking improves my mood and recharges me.

examples.ko: 다음 주를 위해 에너지를 재충전할 거예요.
examples.en: I will recharge my energy for next week.

examples.ko: 잠깐 낮잠을 자고 재충전해서 다시 일했어요.
examples.en: I took a short nap, recharged, and worked again.
If you can't recharge, you get tired quickly.

explain: 배터리 같은 물건에는 '충전하다'가 먼저 떠오르고, 사람이 쉬면서 힘을 되찾을 때는 '재충전하다'가 잘 어울려요. 일이나 공부 사이의 휴식을 말할 때 '재충전의 시간'이라는 표현도 써요.

phrases.en: This vacation was a time to recharge for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬면서 힘을 되찾는 시간을 명사처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a noun phrase for a time of rest and renewal.

phrases.example: 너무 피곤해서 며칠 쉬면서 재충전하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I'm so tired that I want to rest a few days and recharge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬고 싶은 마음을 말할 때 '-고 싶다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combine with -고 싶다 to say you want to rest and renew yourself.

phrases.en: I went on a trip and recharged my energy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 되찾는지 '에너지'로 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names what you regain: energy.

explain_en: For objects like batteries, 충전하다 comes to mind first, while 재충전하다 fits a person resting and getting their strength back. You will also hear the phrase 재충전의 시간 for a break between work or study.

examples.en: He beat his rival with an excellent scheme.
I was completely fooled by the other team's trick.
We need a new strategy for this election.

examples.ko: 감독은 우승을 위해 치밀한 책략을 짰어요.
examples.en: The coach devised a careful scheme to win the championship.

examples.ko: 겉으로는 친절하지만 다 책략일 수 있어요.
examples.en: He seems kind on the surface, but it could all be a ploy.

examples.ko: 역사 속 책략가들의 이야기를 읽는 게 재미있어요.
examples.en: I enjoy reading stories about schemers in history.

explain: 목표를 이루려고 미리 짜 둔 꾀를 말하고, '책략을 쓰다', '책략을 짜다'처럼 말해요. '계략'과 거의 비슷하고, '전략'은 목표를 이루는 큰 계획이라 '책략'보다 속이는 느낌이 덜해요.

phrases.example: 감독이 경기 전에 새로운 책략을 짰어요.
phrases.en: The coach worked out a new scheme before the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획을 미리 준비한다는 뜻으로, 표제어와 가장 자주 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means preparing a plan in advance; the most common pairing.

phrases.en: He used a clever trick and won the contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짜 둔 꾀를 실제로 사용할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when actually putting a prepared trick into action.

phrases.en: They fell for the enemy's scheme.
phrases.nuance_ko: '책략'과 거의 비슷하지만 남을 속이려는 느낌이 조금 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same, but with a stronger sense of deceiving others.

explain_en: Tactical move to win or outwit, e.g. in games (경기) It means a cunning plan worked out in advance to reach a goal, used as '책략을 쓰다' or '책략을 짜다'. It is close to '계략', while '전략' is a bigger plan for reaching a goal and feels less like trickery than '책략'.

t90.ax: We need a new strategy for this election.

en: to desire; to covet; to crave

examples.en: He doesn't covet other people's property.
He lost his friends by craving a high position.

examples.ko: 욕심을 부려 남의 것을 탐하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't be greedy and covet what belongs to others.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 돈만 탐해서 인기가 없어요.
examples.en: He only craves money, so he isn't popular.
He has never sought fame.
My little brother covets his older brother's toys.

explain: 갖고 싶어서 욕심을 낸다는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 재물, 권력, 명예 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '욕심내다'가 더 편하게 들려요.

phrases.en: He is not someone who craves wealth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '탐하다'와 가장 잘 어울리는 짝말 중 하나예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is one of the most natural collocations with 탐하다.

phrases.example: 남의 것을 탐하는 마음은 버려야 해요.
phrases.en: You should give up a greedy desire for others' things.
phrases.nuance_ko: '탐하는 + 명사'로 욕심을 부정적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '탐하는 + noun' talks about greed in a negative way.

phrases.en: Don't be greedy for other people's things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '탐하다' 대신 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the easier everyday word to use instead of 탐하다.

explain_en: It carries a negative feeling of greedily wanting something. It goes well with words like wealth, power and fame. In everyday talk, '욕심내다' sounds more casual.

en: to complain; to whine; to vent

examples.ko: 친구가 회사 일이 힘들다고 한참 하소연했어요.
examples.en: My friend poured out for a long while how hard work at the company is.

examples.ko: 어디에 하소연해도 들어 주는 사람이 없었어요.
examples.en: No matter where I complained, nobody listened.

examples.ko: 하소연할 사람이 없어서 일기에 마음을 적었어요.
examples.en: I had no one to vent to, so I wrote my feelings in a diary.

examples.ko: 엄마한테 하소연하고 나니 마음이 좀 풀렸어요.
examples.en: After venting to my mom, I felt a bit better.
A customer was in front of the shop pleading that it was unfair.

examples.ko: 그만 하소연하지 말고 해결책을 같이 찾아봐요.
examples.en: Let's stop complaining and look for a solution together.

explain: '불평하다'가 싫은 점을 말하는 거라면, 하소연하다는 억울하거나 힘든 사정을 누군가에게 털어놓으며 이해해 주길 바라는 느낌이 있어요. '푸념하다'와 비슷하지만 하소연은 듣는 사람이 정해져 있는 경우가 많아요. 명사 '하소연'은 '하소연을 하다/듣다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: On the way home, I grumbled to my friend about having so much work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하소연과 비슷하지만 듣는 사람이 꼭 정해져 있지 않고 혼잣말 같은 느낌도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but the listener need not be specific, and it can sound like muttering.

phrases.en: He went on and on with his complaints for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '하소연'을 써서 길게 털어놓는다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 하소연 to stress pouring it all out at length.

phrases.en: I had no one to complain to, so I endured it alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 털어놓을 사람이나 곳이 없을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair used when there is nobody or nowhere to vent to.

explain_en: Telling someone your hardships to get sympathy; spoken, emotional. While '불평하다' is about voicing dislikes, 하소연하다 means pouring out an unfair or hard situation to someone, hoping they understand. It is close to '푸념하다', but 하소연 usually has a particular listener. The noun appears often as '하소연을 하다/듣다'.

t90.ax: After venting to my mom, I felt a bit better.

examples.ko: 공원에서 두 사람이 갈퀴로 낙엽을 모으고 있어요.
examples.en: Two people are gathering fallen leaves with rakes in the park.
Grandfather went out to the yard carrying a rake.
Do you know where the rake is in the shed?

examples.ko: 갈퀴 끝이 부러져서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: The tines of the rake broke, so I have to buy a new one.

examples.ko: 이 갈퀴는 가벼워서 어린이도 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: This rake is light, so even children can use it.

examples.ko: 풀을 모을 때는 빗자루보다 갈퀴가 편해요.
examples.en: For gathering grass, a rake is more convenient than a broom.

explain: 낙엽, 마른풀, 짚처럼 가벼운 것을 긁어모으는 도구예요. 바닥을 쓰는 '빗자루'와 달리 끝이 갈라져 있어서 마당이나 밭일에 써요.

phrases.en: I raked the yard on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갈퀴로 긁어모으는 일을 하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the act of raking things together with a rake.

phrases.en: I raked the straw in the yard into a pile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 '으로' 써서 가벼운 것을 한곳에 모을 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the tool with '으로' to gather light things into one place.

explain_en: It is a tool for raking together light things like fallen leaves, dry grass and straw. Unlike a '빗자루' (broom) for sweeping floors, it has split tines and is used for yard and field work.

examples.ko: 배의 돛대에 큰 깃발이 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A big flag hangs from the ship's mast.
The wind was so strong that the mast almost broke.
The sailor climbed up the mast.

examples.ko: 돛대 위에서 멀리 있는 섬을 찾았어요.
examples.en: From the top of the mast, I spotted a faraway island.

examples.ko: 저 돛대는 높이가 이십 미터가 넘어요.
examples.en: That mast is more than twenty meters tall.
They lowered all the sails, leaving only the mast.

explain: '돛'은 바람을 받는 천이고, '돛대'는 그 돛을 다는 기둥이에요. 두 말을 헷갈리기 쉬운데, '돛을 올리다/내리다'처럼 돛에는 올리고 내린다고 말해요.

phrases.en: We put up a new mast on the ship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돛을 달 기둥을 만들어 세울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for setting up the pole that carries the sail.

phrases.en: The sailor climbed the mast and looked far into the distance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 곳에서 먼 곳을 볼 때 돛대에 오른다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Climbing the mast is how sailors get a high view of far-off places.

phrases.en: A bird is sitting at the top of the mast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기둥의 가장 높은 곳을 말할 때 '꼭대기'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '꼭대기' to name the very top of the pole.

explain_en: '돛' is the cloth that catches the wind, and '돛대' is the pole that holds it. They are easy to mix up, but you say '돛을 올리다/내리다' (raise/lower the sail) for the sail itself.

examples.ko: 겨울이 오기 전에 땔감을 미리 준비해 둬야 해요.
examples.en: You have to prepare firewood in advance before winter comes.

examples.ko: 산에서 땔감을 구해 오는 건 할아버지 일이었어요.
examples.en: Gathering firewood from the mountain was Grandfather's job.

examples.ko: 이 나무는 젖어서 땔감으로 쓰기 어려워요.
examples.en: This wood is wet, so it's hard to use as fuel.

examples.ko: 시골집 마당에는 아직도 땔감이 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: There is still firewood piled up in the yard of the country house.

examples.ko: 땔감이 떨어져서 아궁이에 불을 못 피웠어요.
examples.en: We ran out of firewood, so we couldn't light the fire in the stove.
My father splits logs and uses them as fuel.

explain: 불을 때는 데 쓰는 나무나 풀을 가리킬 때가 많아요. 전기나 가스가 아니라 장작·솔가지처럼 직접 불을 피우는 재료를 말할 때 어울려요. '연료'는 더 넓은 말이라 자동차나 기계에도 쓰지만, '땔감'은 아궁이·난로·모닥불 이야기에서 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 눈이 오기 전에 땔감을 구해야 해요.
phrases.en: We have to get firewood before it snows.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땔감을 찾아 마련한다는 뜻으로, 겨울 준비 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means finding and getting fuel, often in talk about preparing for winter.

phrases.en: We use dry branches as firewood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 불 피우는 재료로 쓴다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something serves as material for making a fire.

phrases.en: We ran out of firewood, so the room is cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땔감이 다 없어졌을 때 쓰는 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural way to say the fuel has run out.

explain_en: It most often refers to wood or brush used to make a fire. It fits things you burn directly, like logs and pine twigs, rather than electricity or gas. '연료' (fuel) is broader and also applies to cars and machines, while '땔감' sounds natural when talking about stoves, fireplaces and campfires.

en: with a scrubbing sound; scrubbing hard

examples.en: You have to rub the sleeves hard to get the dirt out.
I scrubbed the soles of my sneakers hard with a toothbrush.
I scrubbed the bottom of the pot hard with a scouring pad.
My head itched, so I scratched it hard.
My hands are dirty, so I'm scrubbing them hard with soap.
There was a sound of someone scraping the wallpaper off.

explain: 힘을 주어 문지르거나 긁거나 씻을 때 나는 소리와 모양이에요. 반대로 부드럽게 할 때는 '살살'이라고 해요. '빡빡'은 더 세고 거친 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I scrubbed the bathroom floor hard, and it became clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘을 줘서 문질러 때를 없앨 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for scrubbing hard to remove dirt.

phrases.en: My back was itchy, so I scratched it hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가려운 곳을 세게 긁는 모습에도 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also fits well for scratching an itch vigorously.

phrases.en: I rubbed my hands hard to wash them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '닦다'보다 손으로 세게 비비는 동작이 더 잘 보이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the hard rubbing motion of the hands more clearly than '닦다'.

explain_en: It imitates the sound and look of rubbing, scratching or washing with force. The opposite, for gentle action, is '살살'. '빡빡' feels even stronger and rougher.

t90.ax: My head itched, so I scratched it hard.

examples.en: My back itched, so I scratched it hard with my nails.
The child tore the drawing paper with a ripping sound.
Dad swept the yard hard with a broom.

examples.ko: 지우개로 북북 문질러도 잘 안 지워져요.
examples.en: Even when I rub it hard with an eraser, it doesn't come off well.
I scratched my head hard while thinking.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 편지를 북북 찢어 버렸어요.
examples.en: I was angry, so I ripped the letter to pieces.

explain: 거칠게 긁거나 찢거나 문지를 때 나는 소리와 모습이에요. '박박'은 닦거나 긁을 때 쓰고, 종이나 천을 찢을 때는 '북북'이 더 자연스러워요. '긁다, 찢다, 문지르다' 같은 동사 앞에 와요.

phrases.en: I scratched the mosquito bite hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가려운 곳을 거칠게 긁을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when scratching an itch roughly.

phrases.en: My younger sibling ripped the letter to pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이나 천을 거칠게 찢을 때 쓰는 가장 자연스러운 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing for roughly tearing paper or cloth.

phrases.en: I rubbed the stain hard, but it won't come off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘을 줘서 거칠게 문지를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when rubbing something hard and roughly.

explain_en: It describes the sound and look of scratching, tearing or rubbing roughly. '박박' is used for scrubbing or scratching, but for ripping paper or cloth, '북북' is more natural. It comes before verbs like '긁다', '찢다' and '문지르다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling took apart a clock, and our parents were surprised.
Over time, microbes break down food waste.
I learned how to take a computer apart from a video.

examples.ko: 분해할 때는 나사를 잃어버리지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: When you take it apart, be careful not to lose the screws.

examples.ko: 분해한 부품을 다시 조립하기가 쉽지 않았어요.
examples.en: It wasn't easy to put the parts I took apart back together.

examples.ko: 이 장난감은 분해하면 여섯 조각이 돼요.
examples.en: This toy comes apart into six pieces.

explain: 기계나 물건을 부품으로 나눌 때, 그리고 물질이 작게 나뉠 때 모두 써요. 다시 맞추는 것은 '조립하다'라서 둘은 짝이에요. 구어로는 '뜯다'도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I took apart the broken radio to look inside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분해하다'보다 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, spoken alternative to '분해하다'.

phrases.en: Plastic doesn't break down easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분해하다'의 피동형으로, 물질이 저절로 작게 나뉠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form is for substances that break down on their own.

phrases.en: I put the toy I took apart back together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분해하다'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '분해하다'.

explain_en: It covers both taking a machine or object apart and a substance breaking down into smaller parts. Putting it back together is 조립하다, so the two are a pair. In casual speech people also say 뜯다.

examples.en: The kids made glasses out of red cellophane paper.

examples.ko: 셀로판지를 눈앞에 대면 세상이 다른 색으로 보여요.
examples.en: If you hold cellophane paper in front of your eyes, the world looks a different color.

examples.ko: 이 셀로판지는 너무 얇아서 자꾸 찢어져요.
examples.en: This cellophane paper is so thin that it keeps tearing.

examples.ko: 창문에 분홍 셀로판지를 붙이니 방이 따뜻해 보여요.
examples.en: With pink cellophane paper on the window, the room looks warm.

examples.ko: 선물을 투명한 셀로판지에 싸고 리본을 묶었어요.
examples.en: I wrapped the gift in clear cellophane paper and tied a ribbon.

examples.ko: 셀로판지 한 장만 빌려줄 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you lend me just one sheet of cellophane paper?

explain: 얇고 빛이 비치는 포장·공작 재료예요. 색깔 셀로판지를 눈이나 손전등에 대고 노는 만들기 수업에 자주 나와요. 줄여서 '셀로판'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I decorated the window nicely with cellophane.
phrases.nuance_ko: '셀로판지'를 줄인 말이라서 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of '셀로판지', used in casual speech.

phrases.en: I stuck blue cellophane paper on the flashlight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색 이름과 함께 써서 어떤 색인지 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with a color word to say which color it is.

phrases.en: I wrapped the candy in cellophane paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선물이나 간식을 얇고 투명하게 싸는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for wrapping gifts or snacks in thin, clear paper.

explain_en: It is a thin, see-through material used for wrapping and crafts. Colored sheets often appear in craft classes, held over eyes or flashlights. It is also shortened to '셀로판'.
